subject: PrivOffer: GreenByte APAC tax harmonization & rev-share escalation
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivOffer: GreenByte APAC tax harmonization & rev-share ask

Team — quick escalation. GreenByte (Sara) is ready to take a private offer on AWS for multi-region APAC listing but they have three non-standard asks that are blocking legal/procurement signoff. I need exec approval to move forward with a bespoke offer. Summary: 

- Customer: GreenByte Analytics (series B; advanced analytics for retail)
- Commercial ask: multi-year commit (24 months) with $150k upfront credit + Net-60 payment terms (they asked Net-90)
- Marketplace ask: APAC-only rev-share reduction request to 12% (our standard for this channel is 18%–20%) citing large commit and regional go-to-market co-funding
- Tax/finance ask: local invoicing preference (GreenByte will invoice our Singapore entity) and they request Redwood to accept supplier gross-up treatment for withholding taxes in PH/ID/NZ (they want us to bear gross-up)

Attachments: GreenByte_SOW_Markup_20260726.pdf, APAC_TaxMatrix_v3.xlsx (tax team mapping), GreenByte_PO_202607.pdf

Requested approval (single line): Approve a conditional private offer on AWS with rev-share = 12% (APAC-only), Net-60 payment terms, and acceptance of localized invoicing subject to tax gross-up cap (see options below). If approved we will: 1) require a 24-month minimum commit, 2) stage the $150k credit over first 6 months (non-refundable unless we materially miss SLOs), and 3) push DocuSign SOW with Legal's standard Marketplace addenda.

Why this matters: GreenByte is committing $2.4M TCV over 24 months (projected run-rate $100k+/mo) and is strategic for our retail vertical in APAC. If we decline the rev-share concession they will walk and instead list via direct procurement with a different vendor.

Fallback options (if Exec wants to mitigate risk):
- Option A: Approve 14% rev-share and require 36-month lock + 50% refundable credit holdback
- Option B: Approve 12% rev-share limited to Singapore/AU only (exclude PH/ID until tax treatment clarified)

Ask: Please respond with a decision by EOD tomorrow PDT so we can send DocuSign and coordinate AWS private listing lead time.

Thanks,
Irene
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivOffer: GreenByte APAC tax harmonization & rev-share ask

Irene — thanks for the concise summary. A couple fast questions before I weigh in: 

1) ARR math: can you confirm the $2.4M is TCV recognized via Marketplace billing (i.e., subject to AWS fees) vs direct invoicing? I want to know our net take after marketplace fees and the proposed rev-share change.
2) Tax/gross-up: what are the estimated gross-up exposure numbers for PH/ID? I had a quick look at APAC_TaxMatrix_v3.xlsx but need a high-level estimate to present to finance.
3) Credit staging: can we structure the $150k as service-credit drawdown tied to usage thresholds (reduces churn risk)?

Preliminary view: I’m inclined to support a 12% rev-share only if we: (a) get the 24-month commit and (b) make the $150k conditional (staged), and (c) cap Redwood’s gross-up exposure to a fixed amount (e.g., $12k per jurisdiction) — otherwise the tax liability risk is open-ended.

Marissa — can you run the net take calc and put a recommended approval table (net revenue at 18% vs 14% vs 12% over 24 months) by EOD? I’ll pull Legal to confirm the gross-up language we can accept.

—Karthik
VP, Strategic Accounts
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-26T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivOffer: GreenByte APAC tax harmonization & rev-share ask

Adding the commercial lens + recommendation. Attached is a two-sheet summary (RevenueModel and Sensitivity) and the marked SOW (GreenByte_SOW_Markup_20260726.pdf). High level: 

- Verified TCV: $2.4M over 24 months; expected AWS marketplace fee ~7% of list.
- Net take (approx): 
  - At 18% rev-share: annual net ~ $840k after marketplace fees
  - At 14% rev-share: annual net ~ $920k
  - At 12% rev-share: annual net ~ $960k
- Incremental delta vs standard (18% -> 12%): ~ $120k/year (gross) before tax/gross-up exposure.

Recommendation (approve with constraints):
1) Approve 12% rev-share APAC-only but require a 24-month lock and minimum runway (first 3 months usage floor = $50k)
2) Stage the $150k credit into three tranches tied to usage and onboarding milestones (30/30/40) and make it non-refundable except for confirmed SLO failures
3) Cap Redwood gross-up exposure to $15k total across APAC jurisdictions; anything beyond is customer responsibility (documented in SOW)
4) Require a DocuSign milestone schedule and implement a clawback clause in case of early termination within 12 months

If Exec signs off on the above, I will: 1) finalize the private-offer terms with AWS listing team, 2) prepare a one-pager for Legal to insert the gross-up cap language, and 3) issue the DocuSign to GreenByte.

Irene — I’ve attached the revenue model (APAC_TaxMatrix_v3.xlsx contains the tax flags) and highlighted the gross-up jurisdictions.

—Marissa
Director, Commercial Finance
From: Sara Liu <sara.liu@greenbyte.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@greenbyte.com>
Date: 2026-07-27T02:10:00+08:00
Subject: Re: PrivOffer: GreenByte APAC tax harmonization & rev-share ask

Thanks Irene — appreciate the quick turnaround. GreenByte is happy to accept the outlined constraints with two clarifications: 

1) Gross-up cap: acceptable at $15k total provided Redwood confirms that the cap will be applied per-country in the Philippines and Indonesia (we will need line-by-line tax treatment confirmed for our auditors)
2) Credit staging: 30/30/40 is acceptable. We will sign a 24-month SOW and issue a PO once we have DocuSign. Attached is the PO draft (GreenByte_PO_202607.pdf).

Next steps from our side: please send DocuSign with the SOW + marketplace addenda and a short note confirming the gross-up application per-country. We will countersign within 48 hours once legal confirms the language.

Appreciate you moving fast on this — Singapore launch is coordinated with our retail partner kickoff in early Q4 and timing is important.

Best,
Sara Liu
Head of Partnerships
GreenByte Analytics
